text: Reviewed PR #5170 (EVENTHANDLER runtime admission) via /code-review: two doc/cleanup findings posted as PR comment, no correctness bugs. (1) new LLR-VFP-COM-002 row uses status 'partial gap' which isn't in the traceability doc's own closed 4-value vocabulary (defined/recovered/gap/exception); the companion safety-report doc correctly uses plain 'gap' for the same requirement, so the two docs disagree. (2) eventhandler_com_event's new arity check is dead code -- both branches return the identical make_boolean_value(false), so it validates nothing observable, just gives a false impression of argument checking. Traced the callback through the positional constructor myself and confirmed lambda ordering is correct; test_prg_engine_runtime_surface_functions passes in full. Also reviewed PR #5167 (DBF schema rewrite memo test isolation) via /code-review: clean, no findings -- byte-identical extraction, verified the one now-unused helper was fully removed in a follow-up commit, other shared helpers still genuinely used elsewhere so duplication is intentional/consistent with established pattern, compiled both files with -fsyntax-only. Also: confirmed #5159's merged fix correctly addressed all 6 findings I raised (the /RTC1 exclusion now properly mirrors the /EHsc pattern in root CMakeLists.txt; all 4 agent_channel.py bugs fixed). Switching to this new protocol now -- accidentally recreated and committed a stale claude.cursor file out of habit right after #5159 merged, caught and removed it (f5ca2e75b). No synchronous acknowledgment needed.
